[[9 ABY]] {{C|Epilogue}} }} {{Quote|''Star Wars Rebels'' is an adventure show that focuses on a street-smart teenage boy who just might have what it takes to be a Jedi, and who joins a small band of rebels that engages in daring missions of resistance against the evil Galactic Empire.|[[Rayne Roberts]], [[Star Wars Insider 152|''Star Wars Insider'' 152]]|{{InsiderCite|152|Rebel Friends!}}}} '''''Star Wars Rebels''''' is an animated television series set during the [[time]] frame between the films [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. It premiered worldwide as a one-hour television movie, ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'', on [[Disney Channel]] on [[October 3]], [[2014]]; Regular episodes aired for four seasons on [[Disney XD]], from [[October 13]], 2014 to [[March 5]], [[2018]]. During its run, the series was nominated for four [[Wikipedia:Emmy Awards|Emmy Awards]], including two consecutive nominations for "Outstanding Children's Program."{{WebCite|url=https://www.emmys.com/shows/star-wars-rebels|text=Star Wars Rebels AWARDS & NOMINATIONS|work=[https://www.emmys.com emmys.com]|archivedate=20190904082728}} The series follows a motley group of [[Spectres|rebels]] who live aboard the [[VCX-100 light freighter|starship]] ''[[Ghost]]'' as they [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|fight]] the [[Galactic Empire]]. The rebels include [[Ezra Bridger]], a young orphan from [[Lothal]] who learns he can use [[the Force]]; [[Kanan Jarrus]], a [[Jedi]] who survived [[Order 66]]; [[Hera Syndulla]], a [[Twi'lek]] [[pilot]] and veteran resistance fighter; [[Sabine Wren]], a [[Mandalore|Mandalorian]] explosives expert; [[Garazeb Orrelios|Garazeb "Zeb" Orrelios]], a [[Lasat]] warrior; and the cantankerous [[astromech droid]] [[C1-10P]], also known as Chopper. The crew will eventually help give rise to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. Lucasfilm first announced ''Star Wars Rebels'' on [[May 20]], [[2013]], following the news that the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' would be ending and that a new series would be produced. ''Star Wars Rebels'' was the first new major ''Star Wars'' project to be released following [[The Walt Disney Company]]'s acquisition of [[Lucasfilm]] in [[2012]]. The series was created by [[Dave Filoni]], [[Simon Kinberg]], and [[Carrie Beck]], and stars actors [[Taylor Gray]], [[Freddie Prinze Jr.]], [[Vanessa Marshall]], [[Tiya Sircar]], [[Steve Blum]], and Dave Filoni. ==Plot summary== ===Premise=== {{Quote|…we're going to really show the origins of the rebellion. When our series begins, it's not the Rebel Alliance yet; we start with a group of rebels. It'll be really interesting to show the progress of the Alliance forming…|Executive producer Greg Weisman, ''Star Wars Insider'' 146|{{InsiderCite|146|Reigniting the Rebellion!}}}} The series begins five years before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], fourteen [[Standard year|years]] into the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]].{{SW|url=news/nycc-2013-meet-the-inquisitor-the-new-face-of-evil-in-star-wars-rebels|text=NYCC 2013: Meet the Inquisitor, the New Face of Evil in ''Star Wars Rebels''|nobackup=1}}{{Twitter|infinata|status/428247081833070592|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|nobackup=1}} The general premise is described as follows: "It is a dark time in [[the galaxy]], as the evil Galactic Empire tightens its grip of power from [[Planet|world]] to world. As the series begins, Imperial forces have occupied a [[Lothal|remote planet]], ruling with an iron fist and ruining the lives of its people. But there are a select few who are brave enough to stand up against the endless [[Stormtrooper]]s and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] of the Empire: the clever and motley crew of the [[starship]] ''[[Ghost]]''. Together, this ragtag group will face threatening new villains, have thrilling adventures, and become heroes."{{SWArchive|url=news/star-wars-rebels-action-figure-packaging-revealed.html|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' Action Figure Packaging Revealed}} ==Development== ===Conception=== {{Quote|They wanted to do an animated show and I loved [Cartoon Network's] Clone Wars and grew up with a lot of animated shows. So we just started to talk about where it would fall in the general Star Wars timeline. Really there was no predetermination going in. It could have been a prequel, sequel, a stand-alone universe.|Simon Kinberg|{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2014/01/23/star-wars-rebels-interview|text='Star Wars Rebels' interview: New series goes to dark places, embraces 1977 film's spirit|author=Hibberd, James|date=2014-01-23|work=[[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20181201233215}}}} ''Star Wars Rebels'' was created by [[Dave Filoni]], [[Simon Kinberg]], and [[Carrie Beck]]. The concept originated with Beck, who suggested it be about "this [[Wikipedia:The A-Team|A-team]] group that went around righting wrongs." This reminded Filoni of his original concept for ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'',{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/star-wars-rebels-easter-eggs-episode-7|text=Executive Producer Dave Filoni Talks STAR WARS REBELS, the Game Plan for the Show, Easter Eggs, Advances in Animation, and More|author=Radish, Christina|date=2014-10-04|work=[[Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20200109165831}} which he described in ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'': "My rough idea was to deal with a small number of characters [a Jedi Master and Padawan, a smuggler and his girlfriend, and a [[Gungan]] "strongman" called Lunker], have them based on a ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''-style smuggling ship, and involve them in black market trade, war espionage, and other stories that existed outside the giant galactic conflict going on in the background."''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' Discussion of where ''Rebels'' would fall in the ''Star Wars'' timeline led to the decision to center the series on the Rebel Alliance. Thus, the series was placed between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'', during the reign of the Galactic Empire, though not so close to ''A New Hope'' that it would feel repetitive. In contrast to the galaxy-hopping structure of ''The Clone Wars'', it was decided ''Rebels'' would depict the Rebellion from one group of characters' point of view. According to Filoni, Kinberg likened it to imagining a show set during the [[Wikipedia:American Revolution|American Revolution]] "that was about five guys that were locked up in a farmhouse somewhere fighting against the local British military and without any real knowledge of the larger political movements." He also noted how the [[original trilogy]] mentioned events like the dissolution of the [[Imperial Senate]] without depicting them.{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/star-wars-rebels-interview-dave-filoni|text=/Film Interview: 'Star Wars Rebels' Dave Filoni Answers Burning Questions About The New Series|author=Lussier, Germain|date=2014-08-07|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20190719033559}} The development team set out to differentiate the series from ''The Clone Wars'' by basing much of the visuals on the designs of [[Ralph McQuarrie]]—the artist who developed concept art for much of the original trilogy of films. ''Rebels'' was influenced by ideas developed by [[George Lucas]] for ''[[Star Wars: Underworld]]'',{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/story/front/SDCC_2014_Complete_Audio_From_Star_Wars_A_New_Dawn_Panel_159102.asp|text=SDCC 2014: Complete Audio From Star Wars: A New Dawn Panel|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20190830210911}} and much of the action in ''Rebels'' was influenced by the ''[[Indiana Jones]]'' franchise which George Lucas also contributed to.{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/oct/12/star-wars-rebels-disney-dave-filoni|text=Star Wars Rebels: 'A lot of our action is actually inspired by Indiana Jones'|author=Dredge, Stuart|date=2014-10-12|work=[[Wikipedia:The Guardian|''The Guardian'']]|archivedate=20180829072126}} Early in development, Disney wanted a more comedy-oriented series than Lucasfilm was interested in making. Kathleen Kennedy and the ''Rebels'' creative team had to make their case otherwise.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/lucasfilms-kathleen-kennedy-what-george-846858|text=Lucasfilm's Kathleen Kennedy on What George Lucas Thinks of 'Force Awakens,' Plans for 'Indiana Jones'|author=Masters, Kim|date=2015-12-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200622061106}} At one point, Filoni considered involving the [[Death Star plans]] in the show, but abandoned the idea after [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story|''Rogue One'']] began development.{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/news/star-wars-rebels-death-star-connection-details-dave-filoni|text=Initial 'Star Wars Rebels' Ideas Involved Discovering Death Star Plans|author=Cavanaugh, Patrick|date=2018-08-07|work=[https://comicbook.com comicbook.com]|archivedate=20200717194954}} He later planned to have appearances from the [[Death Star]] and [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]], but decided it was best to focus on things that directly affect the ''Ghost'' crew.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2454880/why-star-wars-rebels-didnt-show-the-death-star-in-season-4|text=Why Star Wars Rebels Didn't Show The Death Star In Season 4|author=Hurley, Laura|date=2018-07-31|work=[https://www.cinemablend.com Cinemablend]|archivedate=20190505123507}} ===Production=== {{Quote|It has been great seeing the mind meld between our executive producers Dave Filoni, Simon Kinberg, and Greg Weisman during the writers' conferences. [...] Everyone on the team is so passionate about ''Rebels'', and of course it helps that we are all huge fans of ''Star Wars''!|Athena Portillo, ''Star Wars Insider'' 146|}} [[File:GhostImperialConvoyRaidConcept.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Ralph McQuarrie–inspired concept art of the starship ''Ghost'', chased by TIE fighters.]] [[Lucasfilm]] veteran sculptor [[Darren Marshall]], who worked on ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' prior to its cancellation, developed sculpts for the core characters of ''Star Wars Rebels'' before leaving Lucasfilm in [[June]] [[2013]].{{SW|url=news/sculpting-the-clone-wars-and-star-wars-rebels-with-darren-marshall|text=Sculpting ''The Clone Wars'' and ''Star Wars Rebels'' with Darren Marshall}} By [[December]] 2013, the production crew had finished developing the series' [[Star Wars Rebels Season One|first season]] and had begun animating the first script.{{InsiderCite|146|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} As of January 2014, the scripts for Season One were halfway completed. Voice-recording had been finished for five episodes, with three more episodes undergoing storyboarding, two more undergoing animation, and the first episode undergoing lighting. Sound design was also underway, with a theme in place for the series.{{InsiderCite|147|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} [[Greg Weisman]] joined the project as an executive producer in [[May]] 2013, though the series had been under development well before then.{{WebCite|url=http://scumandvillainyradio.com|text=Gargoyles, Rain, and Rebels (Episode 14 for 2/28/14)|date=2014-02-28|archivedate=20140302015349|nolive=1}} On [[January 17]], animation supervisor [[Keith Kellogg]] announced that the production crew had wrapped up animation on the first episode of the series.{{Twitter|Keith_Kellogg|status/424435812319522816|[[Keith Kellogg]]}} To aid in animating the show, Lucasfilm developed a special tool for [[Wikipedia:Adobe Photoshop|Adobe Photoshop]] that emulates Ralph McQuarrie's artistic style;{{Lucasfilm|url=star-wars-rebels|text=Star Wars Rebels|nolive=1}} the character Zeb Orrelios is based on McQuarie's original concept art for the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]]. The series' look is also inspired by the work of [[Wikipedia:Hayao Miyazaki|Hayao Miyazaki]]—a favorite of Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/tv/showtracker/la-et-st-star-wars-rebels-20140310-story.html|text='Star Wars Rebels': Dave Filoni takes 'Star Wars' back to its roots|date=2014-03-11|work=[[Wikipedia:Los Angeles Times|''Los Angeles Times'']]|archivedate=20181019151350}} Filoni requested that the animation crew look at the Disney film [[Wikipedia:Tangled|''Tangled'']], for which 2D facial expressions were created using 3D animation.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2014/04/20/wondercon-star-wars-rebels-clip-and-new-details-revealed|text=WonderCon: Star Wars Rebels Clip and New Details Revealed|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2014-04-19|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archivedate=20200604020933}} Simon Kinberg wrote the series' first two episodes, which serve as a short story arc to introduce the show's main characters. By [[March]] 2014, the entire first season had been mapped out, and according to Greg Weisman, the series as a whole is organized as a three-act play. The first season serves as the first act of the overall series, while the second and third acts may take more than one season. ''Star Wars Rebels'' was overseen by three executive producers: Dave Filoni, Simon Kinberg, and Greg Weisman.{{InsiderCite|143|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} In addition to Filoni, the ''Rebels'' production team included several crew members returning from ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': [[Athena Yvette Portillo]] as line producer, [[Kilian Plunkett]] as art director, [[Joel Aron]] as CG effects supervisor, Keith Kellogg as animation supervisor, and [[Steward Lee]] as episodic director. Lee, Filoni's longest-running episodic director from ''The Clone Wars'', was joined in directorial duties by brother [[Steven G. Lee]], a veteran of [[LucasArts]]. [[Kevin Kiner]], who was previously the composer for ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'', returned as the new music composer for ''Star Wars Rebels''.{{SW|url=news/wondercon-2014-star-wars-rebels-panel-report|text=WonderCon 2014: ''Star Wars Rebels'' Panel Report}} Lucasfilm hired music producer [[Wikipedia:Flux Pavillion|Flux Pavillion]] to remix Kiner's ''Rebels'' main theme.{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/story/front/Lucasfilm_Commissions_Dubstep_Producer_To_Remix_Star_Wars_Rebels_Theme_160013.asp|text=Lucasfilm Commissions Dubstep Producer To Remix ''Star Wars Rebels'' Theme|author=Geller, Eric|date=2014-09-25|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20180829212058}} Other returning crew members from ''The Clone Wars'' included [[Amy Beth Christenson]], [[Andre Kirk]], [[Pat Presley]], and [[Chris Glenn]] on the concept art team, managed by [[Liz Cummings]], as well as [[Paul Zinnes]] on the development team. [[Pablo Hidalgo]], a member of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]], also worked with the team as a fact-checker. The crew aimed for an overall aesthetic similar to the original trilogy. As such, Joel Aron tried to give the visuals a "grainy look," Matthew Wood used many of the original trilogy's sound effects for the series' soundtrack,{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/09/28/arts/television/star-wars-rebels-emulates-the-trilogy-of-old.html|text=Empire Renewed: 'Star Wars Rebels' Emulates the Trilogy of Old|author=Barnes, Brooks|date=2014-09-25|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']]|archivedate=20190919135718}} and the crew animated the lightsabers in such a way as to emulate the look of those in the original trilogy.{{WebCite|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2014/10/03/star-wars-rebels-lightsabers-exclusive/16633095|text='Rebels' lightsabers reflect 'Star Wars' roots|author=Truitt, Brian|date=2014-10-03|work=[[Wikipedia:USA Today|''USA Today'']]|archivedate=20191215073958}} ==Release and reception== [[File:Rebelspropaganda.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Imperial propaganda poster created to promote the series]] {{Quote|Citizens of Lothal: It is by Imperial Decree that you are requested to proudly display these posters on behalf of your Empire. As loyal residents of one of the Empire's most vital stations on the Outer Rim, your compliance is appreciated. Imperial Service is a noble endeavor which paves the way for your freedom and security. Remember, it is the will of Emperor Palpatine to ensure the future of a stable and prosperous galaxy.|Letter included in the ''Star Wars Rebels'' propaganda poster mailing promotion|{{Twitter|CanadianFanboy|status/430893963789471744|Andy|nobackup=1}}}} ''Star Wars Rebels'' was first announced on [[March 11]], 2013, as an unnamed animated series set to replace ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''.{{SW|url=news/a-new-direction-for-lucasfilm-animation|text=A New Direction for Lucasfilm Animation}} Its name and fall 2014 premiere were announced in a press release on [[May 20]], 2013. The six card backs, when combined together, formed the ''Rebels'' phoenix logo.{{Twitter|RebelsReport|status/431056504523747329|quote=The back of the limited edition set of Rebels propaganda cards make up the #StarWarsRebels Thunderbird logo|Rebels Report}} Starting with Chopper, the "grumpy astromech droid" on [[January 28]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-meet-chopper-grumpy-astromech-droid|text=Star Wars Rebels: Meet Chopper, Grumpy Astromech Droid}} a series of videos was released that introduced each of the crew members of the ''Ghost''. Kanan was introduced as "the Cowboy Jedi" on [[February 12]], and "the Street-Smart Hero" Ezra Bridger followed on [[February 14]]. Two ''Rebels'' teasers, entitled "Spark" and "Ignite," were released on [[February 17]],{{SWYouTube|1cAwLmyARpE|"Spark" Teaser | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-spark-teaser}}{{SWYouTube|qogqaJ2aXQc|Ignite - Teaser | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-ignite-teaser}} and videos introducing Garazeb Orrelios, "the Muscle," Sabine Wren, "the Explosive Artist," and Hera Syndulla, "the Pilot," were released on [[February 18]], [[February 19|19]], and [[February 20|20]] respectively. The videos were released by independent news sources such as ''TV Guide'', IGN, and ''Entertainment Weekly'', and then were posted on the official ''Star Wars'' YouTube channel shortly afterwards.{{WebCite|url=http://www.tvguide.com/News/Star-Wars-Rebels-Ezra-1077773.aspx|text=First Look: A New Recruit for ''Star Wars Rebels''|author=Sandis, Rich|date=2014-02-14|work=[[Wikipedia:TV Guide|TV Guide]]|archivedate=20191206122706}} On [[April 16]], in conjunction with a following panel at [[Wikipedia:WonderCon|WonderCon 2014]], a clip featuring the character Hera Syndulla was released on the ''Star Wars'' YouTube channel. [[File:RebelsPoster.png|thumb|right|200px|''Star Wars Rebels'' movie-style poster, released in advance of San Diego Comic-Con 2014]] The first full-length trailer for ''Rebels'' was released on May 4, 2014. Known as "The Heroes of ''Star Wars Rebels''," the panel featured Dave Filoni, Simon Kinberg, and the series' principal voice cast.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-and-more-at-san-diego-comic-con-2014|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' and More at San Diego Comic-Con 2014 - So we want the show to work for that group, the most extreme fanboys out there. At the same time, we also have the responsibility that for a certain generation of kids, this is going to be their first exposure to Star Wars.|Greg Weisman|}} Lucasfilm's Pablo Hidalgo first provided a timeline for ''Star Wars Rebels'' of approximately fourteen years after the events of ''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'', which corresponds to around five years before the events of ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. Although the official [[StarWars.com]] press release announcing the ''Rebels'' character Chopper later alternatively stated a timeline of four years prior to the events of ''A New Hope'', Hidalgo quickly reaffirmed the original timeframe via Twitter. Lee]] *[[Steward Lee]] *[[Justin Ridge]]{{Rebels|Art Attack}} |executive producers=*Dave Filoni *Simon Kinberg *Greg Weisman |production company= |starring=*[[Freddie Prinze Jr.]] *[[Vanessa Marshall]] *[[Steve Blum]] *[[Tiya Sircar]] *[[Taylor Gray]] *Dave Filoni *[[David Oyelowo]] *[[Jason Isaacs]] *[[Liam O'Brien]] *[[David Shaughnessy]] *[[Dee Bradley Baker]] *[[Stephen Stanton]] |timeline=[[5 BBY]]–[[4 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' |preceded by= |followed by=[[Star Wars Rebels Season Two|''Star Wars Rebels'' Season Two]] }} '''''Star Wars Rebels'' Season One''' is the first season of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. The season premiered on [[October 3]], [[2014]] on the [[Disney Channel]], beginning with the one-hour television movie ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''. The full series began on [[Disney XD]] with the premiere of the episode "[[Droids in Distress]]" on [[October 13]], and it ended with "[[Fire Across the Galaxy]]" on [[March 2]], [[2015]]. The season is executive produced by [[Dave Filoni]], [[Simon Kinberg]], and [[Greg Weisman]]. Set five years before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first season follows the [[Spectres|crew]] of the starship ''[[Ghost]]'' in the early days of the fight against the [[Galactic Empire]]. The crew attracts the attention of [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus|Kallus]] of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]], who wants to eliminate them as a threat before they can spark a wider rebellion, and [[the Grand Inquisitor]], a [[Dark side of the Force|dark sider]] who is tasked with killing any [[Jedi]] who survived [[Order 66]]—including [[Kanan Jarrus]] and his new [[Padawan|apprentice]], [[Ezra Bridger]]. The crew of the ''Ghost'' will eventually help form the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. ==Development== The first episode of the series was scripted and had begun the animation process by [[December]] [[2013]].{{InsiderCite|146|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} By [[January]] 2014, Season One's scripts had been halfway completed, with voice recording finished for five episodes and other episodes in various stages of production.{{InsiderCite|147|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} On [[January 17]], animation supervisor [[Keith Kellogg]] announced that the first episode had been fully animated.{{Twitter|Keith_Kellogg|status/424435812319522816|[[Keith Kellogg]]|quote=Just finished animation on the first episode of #StarWarsRebels. Can't wait for you all to see it.}} On [[May 9]], 2014, Simon Kinberg confirmed that season one would contain 16 episodes (released as four shorts, a movie, and 13 episodes), and that he had personally written the first two episodes (which were later rebranded as a movie) as well as the season finale.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/star-wars-rebels-details-simon-kinberg|text=Writer-Producer Simon Kinberg Talks STAR WARS REBELS, His Duties on the Show, and the Thrill of Writing for Original Trilogy Characters|author=Goldberg, Matt|date=2014-05-09|work=Collider|archivedate=20200701055637}} ==Media== {{Mediacat|from=1|imagecat=Images from Star Wars Rebels Season One|soundcat=Audio files from Star Wars Rebels Season One}} ===Episodes=== {|class="wikitable sortable" {{Prettytable}} |- bgcolor="#CCCCCC" ! the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. The season premiered with a one-hour television movie, "[[The Siege of Lothal]]", on [[June 20]], [[2015]]. Regular episodes premiered on [[October 14]], 2015 with the airing of "[[The Lost Commanders]]." ==Development== ===Production=== The production on the second season of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' was officially confirmed on [[October 2]], [[2014]], one day before the release of the series premiere movie, ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''. [[Star Wars Rebels Season One|Season One]] executive producers and series creators [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Simon Kinberg]] continued their creative roles during the second season, while executive producer [[Greg Weisman]] left the series after the completion of the first.{{WebCite|url=https://www.newsarama.com/22286-star-wars-rebels-gets-season-2-ahead-of-premiere-but-with-creative-shifts.html|text=UPDATE: Weisman Leaves STAR WARS REBELS After Season 1, Season 2 Officially Announced|author=Siegal, Lucas|date=2014-10-02|work=Newsarama|archivedate=20191026063829}} Series supervising writer [[Henry Gilroy]] took his place as co-executive producer. [[Freddie Prinze Jr.]], who voices [[Kanan Jarrus]] on the show, revealed that the cast had recorded "nearly twice as many episodes" as the first season,{{Twitter|RealFPJr|status/561194976974233600|[[Freddie Prinze Jr.]]|date=2015-01-30|quote=#StarWarsRebels I cant wait for season 2 to start for you guys. We recorded nearly twice as many episodes. You guys are gonna love it!|archivedate=20170106094123|archivefile=File:FreddiePrinzeJr-RebelsSeason2-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} with the official season having 20 episodes, and one [[The Siege of Lothal|television movie]].{{WebCite|url=http://rebelsreport.com/2015/04/24/star-wars-rebels-season-two-details-the-facts-we-know-so-far|text=Star Wars Rebels Season Two Details: The Facts We Know So Far|archivedate=20150506074918}} ==Release and reception== On [[December 11]], 2014, it was announced that the premiere episode of season two would debut at [[Celebration Anaheim (2015)|Celebration Anaheim]] from [[April]] 16 to 19, [[2015]]. The premiere was followed by an encore screening of season one's last two episodes, as well as a panel featuring Filoni, Prinze Jr., [[Vanessa Marshall]] ([[Hera Syndulla]]), [[Tiya Sircar]] ([[Sabine Wren]]), [[Steve Blum]] ([[Garazeb Orrelios]]), and [[Taylor Gray]] ([[Ezra Bridger]]). The panel also featured an extended look at more content from the second season.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-cast-confirmed-for-star-wars-celebration-2015|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' Season 2 Premiere, Cast Panel, and More Confirmed for ''Star Wars'' Celebration 2015}} After the panel at Celebration Anaheim, it was confirmed that the season would premiere with a one-hour movie in the summer, with episodes airing on [[Disney XD]] in the fall.{{WebCite|url=http://rebelsreport.com/2015/04/18/star-wars-celebration-star-wars-rebels-season-two-press-release|text=Star Wars Celebration Star Wars Rebels Season Two Press Release|archivedate=20160406192214}} On [[April 30]], 2015, the premiere date of the movie, "[[The Siege of Lothal]]", was revealed to be June 20, 2015. On [[August 28]], 2015, it was announced that the episodic premiere would be on [[October 14]], 2015. By the end of October 2015, major development of the season had been completed, with only minor tweaking still in place thereafter.{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/simon-kinberg-discusses-star-wars-rebels-season-2-and-potential-for-characters-to-jump-to-live-action|text=Simon Kinberg Discusses Star Wars Rebels Season 2 and Potential for Characters to Jump to Live-Action|author=Ratcliffe, Amy|date=2015-10-02|work=Nerdist|archivedate=20180616022552}} ==Media== {{Mediacat|from=1|imagecat=Images from Star Wars Rebels Season Two|soundcat=Audio files from Star Wars Rebels Season Two}} ===Episodes=== {|class="wikitable sortable" {{Prettytable}} |- bgcolor="#CCCCCC" ! The season premiered with a one-hour television movie, "[[Steps Into Shadow]]", on [[September 24]], [[2016]]. Regular episodes premiered on [[October 1]], 2016 with the airing of "[[The Holocrons of Fate]]." For this season, [[Dave Filoni]] stepped down as supervising director, replaced by [[Justin Ridge]].{{WebCite|url=https://bigshinyrobot.com/star-wars/star-wars-rebels-filoni-no-longer-supervising-director|text='Star Wars Rebels:' Filoni No Longer Supervising Director|author=Young, Bryan|date=2016-09-23|archivedate=20200319230510}} ==Official description== ''Having established a secret base on Atollon, the ''Ghost'' crew, now led by a more powerful Ezra, strengthens the rebel fleet by acquiring new resources and recruits eager to stand against the Empire. However, the Imperial efforts to eliminate the rebellion are now being led by the coldly analytical Grand Admiral Thrawn, whose strategic, tactical and cultural insights make him a threat unlike any they have faced before. But we never imagined it would end like this.|Hera Syndulla|{{SWYouTube|-b7GAhnVwhA|Star Wars Rebels Season 4 Trailer (Official)|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-season-4-trailer}}}} '''''Star Wars Rebels'' Season Four''' is the fourth and final season of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. It was announced on [[March 3]], [[2017]], and debuted on [[Disney XD]] on [[October 16]]. As with all previous seasons, this one is also began with special two-part episode, called ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore|Heroes of Mandalore]]''. At [[Celebration Orlando]], [[Dave Filoni]], series creator and executive producer, confirmed that it was the final season of the series. He said that it was his decision to end here and very glad to give a proper ending to the series, unlike in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']]. According to Filoni, it is darker and a bit funnier than the previous one.{{SW|url=news/swco-2017-8-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-rebels-season-4-panel|text=SWCO 2017: 8 Things We Learned from the ''Star Wars Rebels'' Season Four Panel}} Voice recording began by [[August]] of [[2016]].{{YouTube|video=q51Stzk_Oz8|text=Star Wars Rebels Season 3 Freddie Prinze Jr FULL Interview [Dash Star]|channel=N/A|name=N/A|nobackup=1}} Filoni later added that, with it being the final season, everything was magnified and nothing could be wasted.
